passages.text: Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
passages.sermon: God has shown us mercy.\r\nGod has given us this ministry.\r\nWe do not lose heart.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἔχοντες τὴν διακονίαν ταύτην καθὼς ἠλεήθημεν οὐκ ἐγκακοῦμεν

passages.text: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Jesus Christ.
We have rejected secret and shameful ways.
We do not act with deceit.
We do not distort the word of God.
We openly proclaim the truth.
We present ourselves honestly to every person’s conscience.
We do this before God.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀπειπάμεθα τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης μὴ περιπατοῦντες ἐν πανουργίᾳ μηδὲ δολοῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τῇ φανερώσει τῆς ἀληθείας συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς πᾶσαν συνείδησιν ἀνθρώπων ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul preaches the gospel.
Some people cannot see or understand the gospel.
The gospel is hidden from these people.
These people are perishing.
If our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔστιν κεκαλυμμένον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἡμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις ἐστὶν κεκαλυμμένον

passages.text: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
passages.sermon:
The god of this age acts now.
He has blinded the minds of unbelievers.
Unbelievers cannot see the light of the gospel.
This gospel shows the glory of Christ.
Christ is the image of God.
passages.original: ἐν οἷς ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἐτύφλωσεν τὰ νοήματα τῶν ἀπίστων εἰς τὸ μὴ αὐγάσαι τὸν φωτισμὸν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς δόξης τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
passages.sermon: We do not proclaim ourselves.\r\nWe proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord.\r\nWe are your servants because of Jesus.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς κηρύσσομεν ἀλλὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν Κύριον ἑαυτοὺς δὲ δούλους ὑμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God spoke at the beginning.
God said, “Let light shine out of darkness.”
God made His light shine in our hearts.
God did this to give us light.
This light is the knowledge of the glory of God.
We see this glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ὁ εἰπών Ἐκ σκότους φῶς λάμψει ὃς ἔλαμψεν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν προσώπῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
passages.sermon:
We have this treasure.
We keep it in jars of clay.
God gives us this treasure.
This treasure shows God’s great power.
This power does not come from us.
This power comes from God.
passages.original: Ἔχομεν δὲ τὸν θησαυρὸν τοῦτον ἐν ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν ἵνα ἡ ὑπερβολὴ τῆς δυνάμεως ᾖ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ μὴ ἐξ ἡμῶν

passages.text: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
passages.sermon:
We are hard pressed on all sides.
We are not crushed.
We are perplexed.
We are not in despair.
We are persecuted.
We are not forsaken.
We are struck down.
We are not destroyed.
passages.original: ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐ στενοχωρούμενοι ἀπορούμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐξαπορούμενοι διωκόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγκαταλειπόμενοι καταβαλλόμενοι ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἀπολλύμενοι

passages.text: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
passages.sermon: We are followers of Jesus.\r\nWe always carry the death of Jesus in our bodies.\r\nWe do this so that the life of Jesus will also be shown in our bodies.
passages.original: πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι ἡμῶν φανερωθῇ

passages.text: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
passages.sermon:
We are people who live.
We are always handed over to death.
This happens because of Jesus.
God does this so the life of Jesus can be shown in our mortal body.
passages.original: ἀεὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες εἰς θάνατον παραδιδόμεθα διὰ Ἰησοῦν ἵνα καὶ ἡ ζωὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ φανερωθῇ ἐν τῇ θνητῇ σαρκὶ ἡμῶν

passages.text: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the believers in Corinth.
Paul and his companions suffer for Jesus.
Death is at work in Paul and his companions.
Life is at work in the believers in Corinth.
passages.original: ὥστε ὁ θάνατος ἐν ἡμῖν ἐνεργεῖται ἡ δὲ ζωὴ ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak, knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
passages.sermon:
We have the same spirit of faith.
Scripture says, "I believed, therefore I have spoken."
We also believe.
Therefore, we also speak.
We know that God raised the Lord Jesus.
God will also raise us with Jesus.
God will present us together with you in His presence.
passages.original: Ἔχοντες δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πίστεως κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον Ἐπίστευσα διὸ ἐλάλησα καὶ ἡμεῖς πιστεύομεν διὸ καὶ λαλοῦμεν εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ ἐγείρας τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ καὶ παραστήσει σὺν ὑμῖν

passages.text: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.
passages.sermon:
God does everything for your benefit.
God gives grace to more and more people.
This grace causes thanksgiving to increase.
This thanksgiving brings glory to God.
passages.original: τὰ γὰρ πάντα δι’ ὑμᾶς ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσασα διὰ τῶν πλειόνων τὴν εὐχαριστίαν περισσεύσῃ εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Jesus Christ.
We do not lose heart.
Our outer self is wasting away.
Our inner self is being renewed every day.
passages.original: Διὸ οὐκ ἐγκακοῦμεν ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ ὁ ἔξω ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος διαφθείρεται ἀλλ’ ὁ ἔσω ἡμῶν ἀνακαινοῦται ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal glory that is far beyond comparison.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Christians in Corinth.
Paul describes suffering as light and momentary.
This suffering is affliction.
This affliction is not permanent.
This affliction is not heavy.
This affliction produces something for us.
It produces eternal glory.
This glory lasts forever.
This glory is far greater than our suffering.
This glory cannot be compared to our affliction.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν αἰώνιον βάρος δόξης κατεργάζεται ἡμῖν

passages.text: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
passages.sermon:
We do not look at things we can see.
We look at things we cannot see.
Things we can see last only a short time.
Things we cannot see last forever.
passages.original: μὴ σκοπούντων ἡμῶν τὰ βλεπόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα τὰ γὰρ βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα τὰ δὲ μὴ βλεπόμενα αἰώνια
